title: Small Talk with an Exchange Student

vocabulary.meaning_en: a student who studies in another country for a short time
vocabulary.example: She is an exchange student from Spain.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the customs, food, art and way of life of a people
vocabulary.example: I want to learn about Arab culture.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a nation with its own land and government

vocabulary.note_ar: be born: I was born in 2005
vocabulary.note_en: Use with "be": I was born in...
born and raised = born and grew up
vocabulary.example: He was born and raised in Kuwait.

vocabulary.meaning_en: leave home to do something fun
a public garden with grass and trees
a small place to buy drinks and light meals
a big building with many shops
vocabulary.example: The shopping mall opens at ten.

vocabulary.meaning_en: old in style and passed down from the past
vocabulary.example: They wear traditional clothes on Eid.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a big, strong old building with walls and towers
use a camera or phone to make photos
vocabulary.example: I like to take pictures of nature.

vocabulary.meaning_en: Saturday and Sunday, or your days off

fine_lines.title: How old vs How long
fine_lines.explanation_ar: How old تسأل عن العمر (How old are you?)، و How long تسأل عن المدة (How long will you stay?).
fine_lines.explanation_en: "How old" asks about age. "How long" asks about time (duration).

examples.sentence: How long will you stay? For one year.

fine_lines.title: I'm from vs I was born in
fine_lines.explanation_ar: I'm from تعني بلدي أو مدينتي الأصلية. I was born in تعني المكان الذي وُلدت فيه (بالماضي).
fine_lines.explanation_en: "I'm from" is your home place. "I was born in" is the place where your life started (past).

expressions.phrase: Where are you from? — I'm from New York.
expressions.meaning_ar: من أين أنت؟ — أنا من نيويورك.
expressions.meaning_en: Ask and answer about home places.
expressions.example: Where are you from? I'm from Tunis.

expressions.phrase: How old are you? — I'm 19 years old.
expressions.example: How old are you? I'm 20 years old.

expressions.phrase: Why are you in Japan? — I'm here as an exchange student.
expressions.meaning_ar: لماذا أنت في اليابان؟ — أنا هنا كطالب تبادل.
expressions.meaning_en: Ask the reason for a visit.
expressions.example: Why are you in Cairo? I'm here as a student.

expressions.meaning_en: Ask how much time someone will stay.
expressions.example: How long will you stay? For two weeks.
One year? That's a long time!

expressions.phrase: I was born and raised in Japan.
expressions.meaning_en: Say where you were born and grew up.
expressions.example: I was born and raised in Riyadh.

expressions.phrase: There's always something new to see.
expressions.example: I love this city. There's always something new to see.

expressions.phrase: Do you want to come with me?
expressions.example: I'm going to the park. Do you want to come with me?
Do you want to come? Sure, I'd love to!

expressions.phrase: I can't wait for the weekend.
expressions.meaning_ar: لا أطيق انتظار عطلة نهاية الأسبوع.
expressions.meaning_en: Say you are excited about something soon.
expressions.example: We are going to the sea. I can't wait for the weekend!

grammar.title: Wh- questions with "be"
grammar.explanation_ar: نسأل بكلمة استفهام + am/is/are + الفاعل: Where are you from? How old are you? Why are you in Japan? والجواب: I'm...
grammar.explanation_en: Wh-word + be + subject: Where are you from? How old are you?
examples: Where are you from? I'm from New York.
Why are you in Japan? I'm here as a student.

grammar.title: Future with "will": How long will you stay?
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم will + الفعل في أصله للحديث عن المستقبل: I will stay for one year. وفي السؤال: How long will you stay?
grammar.explanation_en: Use will + base verb for the future.
examples: How long will you stay in Japan?
I will stay for one year.
We will visit the castle on Saturday.

grammar.title: There is / There are
grammar.explanation_ar: There is للمفرد و There are للجمع لنقول إن شيئًا موجود: There are many parks. There's always something new.
grammar.explanation_en: There is (singular), there are (plural) to say something exists.
examples: There are many parks and cafes.
There's always something new to see.
Are there nice places to go out?

grammar.title: want to + verb
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم want to + الفعل في أصله لنقول ما نريد فعله: I want to visit a castle.
grammar.explanation_en: Use want to + base verb to say what you wish to do.
examples: I want to visit a traditional castle.

questions.question: ___ are you from? — I'm from New York.
How ___ are you? — I'm 19 years old.
How long will you stay in Japan? — I ___ stay for one year.
A student who studies in another country for a short time is an ___.
I was born and ___ in Japan.
___ many parks and cafes in the city.
Do you want to come with me? — ___
questions.explanation_ar: قبول الدعوة: Sure, I'd love to!
questions.explanation_en: To accept: Sure, I'd love to!

questions.question: "I can't wait for the weekend" means...
choices: I'm very excited about the weekend.
I will work at the weekend.
questions.explanation_en: It means you are very excited.
